claims.text: Wear resistance in high-entropy-alloy coatings is primarily governed by formation of a self-adaptive, adherent oxide tribolayer during sliding.
The oxide tribolayer is generated through selective oxidation of elements with high oxygen affinity.
The target materials are physical-vapor-deposited, near-equiatomic multicomponent high-entropy-alloy coatings containing moderate amounts of oxide-forming elements.
The controlled intervention is substitution of approximately 5 at.% of one constituent by Cr or Al.
Cr and Al have strong oxygen affinity.
Increasing the concentration of Cr or Al should enhance in-situ oxide-tribolayer formation.
The proposed comparison uses reciprocating sliding at room temperature in ambient air near 50% relative humidity, approximately 5 N normal load, constant sliding speed, and 5000 cycles.
Tribolayer formation, thickness, and adherence are the structural mediators connecting composition to wear behavior.
Localized frictional heating and mechanical stress during sliding promote selective oxidation of the enriched oxide-forming element.
A thin, adherent oxide tribolayer reduces direct metal-to-metal contact.
The oxide tribolayer mitigates abrasive and adhesive wear by providing self-healing surface protection.
Relative to the baseline coating, the modified coating should have a lower friction coefficient.
Relative to the baseline coating, the modified coating should have a lower wear rate.
The modified coating should develop a thicker, more uniform, and more adherent oxide tribolayer than the baseline coating.
The proposed mechanism should operate under moderate room-temperature ambient-air sliding conditions.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when oxidation is suppressed in vacuum or inert atmospheres.
The proposed mechanism may not apply at extreme temperatures.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies substitution of approximately 5 at.% of an existing constituent, whereas the experimental design describes an additional 5 at.% Cr or Al. Addition and substitution imply different total compositions and do not define the same controlled change.
